beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Israel had walked out of Egypt on a miracle — a sea split open, bread fallen from the sky, water struck out of a rock. But the wilderness was long, and their patience wore through.

timing.text: Israel had walked out of Egypt on a miracle — a sea split open, bread fallen from the sky, water struck out of a rock.
But the wilderness was long, and their patience wore through.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: On the hard road around Edom, tired and discouraged, they turned on the very God who had rescued them, and on Moses.

timing.text: On the hard road around Edom, tired and discouraged, they turned on the very God who had rescued them, and on Moses.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.

timing.text: Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?
for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They had bread from heaven every morning — and called it worthless. And the wilderness they blamed for their misery was about to show them what a real danger looked like.

timing.text: They had bread from heaven every morning — and called it worthless.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.

timing.text: And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The bites spread through the camp. And the same people who had cursed God came running back to Moses, broken.

timing.text: The bites spread through the camp.
And the same people who had cursed God came running back to Moses, broken.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD, and against thee; pray unto the LORD, that he take away the serpents from us.

timing.text: We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD, and against thee; pray unto the LORD, that he take away the serpents from us.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So Moses prayed for the people who had just turned on him. And the LORD answered — but not the way anyone expected.

timing.text: So Moses prayed for the people who had just turned on him.
And the LORD answered — but not the way anyone expected.

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.

timing.text: Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No cure to brew. No ritual to perform. No strength left to muster. Just a shape of bronze lifted on a pole, and one thing left to do — look.

timing.text: No cure to brew.
No ritual to perform.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.

timing.text: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A dying man didn't have to earn it, or explain it, or even understand it. He only had to trust it enough to lift his eyes toward it.

timing.text: A dying man didn't have to earn it, or explain it, or even understand it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Fourteen hundred years later, Jesus reached back and picked this exact moment to explain his own cross.

timing.text: Fourteen hundred years later, Jesus reached back and picked this exact moment to explain his own cross.

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

timing.text: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

card.text: The whole camp was dying, and their healing hung on a pole. All they had to do was look. Look, and live.
